Text:
One single continuous photograph — no panels, grids, or split frames.

PRIORITY ORDER — when instructions conflict, the lower number wins
1. The uploaded image's composition and geometry.
2. The exact people and vehicle counts given below.
3. The historical transformation for the target year.
4. The specific period details listed.
5. Add nothing that is not asked for — no extra businesses, signs, vehicles,
   people, logos or advertisements.

Use the uploaded photo as the exact base composition. The street in the source
is empty — populate it with the people and vehicles specified below. Remove the
modern businesses, logos, brands, storefront names, banners and advertisements
visible in the source image, and replace them only with the period signage
specified below.

PRESERVE
Keep the uploaded image's composition, camera angle, geometry, buildings,
roads and permanent structures exactly as they are. Do not redraw,
reposition or restyle them. Change only what the sections below ask for.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Create a TRUE 9:16 vertical portrait. Expand the SAME scene naturally above
(sky) and below (street/pavement) as canvas extension — do not stretch or
distort the source geometry.

TRANSFORM TO 1995
Clinton era prosperity. An auto repair shop in 1995 — an alignment rack in one bay, an emissions-testing sticker in the window, and a national tire brand banner strung across the apron.

PERIOD DETAILS
- a tire display rack near the office entrance with a hand-lettered '$39.95 ALIGNMENT' sign taped to it
- a parts counter through the glass, computer monitor visible on the desk
- two roll-up bay doors, one open with a car up on an alignment rack
- window signs: 'A/C SERVICE $49.95', 'TIRES — NATIONAL BRANDS'
- a tire display rack near the entrance
- a stack of old tires behind the building
Typography: clean geometric sans-serif, early digital influence.


SIGNAGE RESTRICTION
The only readable text anywhere in the image is:
'$39.95 ALIGNMENT'
'A/C SERVICE $49.95'
'TIRES — NATIONAL BRANDS'
Do not render any other readable words, business names, slogans, advertisements, logos or brand names. Lettering that appears elsewhere must be too small, too distant or too weathered to read as words.

PEOPLE
EXACTLY 4 people TOTAL: 2 near sidewalk (largest, foreground), 1 opposite sidewalk mid-block, 1 distant, far end of block. Grouped in pairs, threes, and singles.
- a mechanic recharging an A/C system with a gauge set
- a man in a cap chatting with the owner at the counter
- a grandmother pushing a wire cart of groceries
Clothing: men in baggy jeans, flannel shirts; women in slip dresses, high-waisted mom jeans. Fashion palette: forest green, maroon, mustard yellow. No posing or eye contact. All people stay on sidewalks, at storefronts, or beside parked vehicles — never standing, sitting, or walking in the road or driving lanes.

VEHICLES
EXACTLY 4 period vehicles, all different:
- 1986-1997 Ford Aerostar — boxy rear-drive minivan — white
- 1992-1995 Pontiac Grand Am — compact with ribbed plastic cladding — black
- 1995-1999 Dodge Neon — small rounded economy, friendly face — teal
- 1994-2001 Dodge Ram — big rig style grille, bold — burgundy
Parked with gaps. Where a model is listed with a year range, render the 1995 model year specifically — only styling, trim and features available in 1995, nothing introduced later. No vehicle newer than 1995.
Parked vehicles sit nose-in or angled into the lot, evenly spaced; none parallel-parked along the street, none blocking a driveway apron. Keep the driveway aprons and the drive lanes through the lot clear.
PLACEMENT: two nose-in near the building; the rest angled into stalls at the far edge of the lot. No vehicle in the same spot as any other era.

ENVIRONMENT
- road markings: yellow center line, white edge lines, turn lane arrows
- utilities: overhead power lines standard, cable TV and early phone data lines on poles

TREES
- maple tree at street corner: clearly smaller than in the base image — about 45% of its canopy there, thinner trunk
- elm tree at side yard: a young tree, only about 25% of its canopy in the base image, thin trunk
Tree sizes MUST follow this specification even where they differ from the base image.

PHOTOGRAPHIC STYLE
COLOR photograph — Kodak Gold 200 or Fujifilm Superia 200 look.
Color: neutral to slightly warm tones. Grain: fine grain, cleaner than 1985.
Photorealistic — NOT black-and-white, no HDR.

PRIVACY
Blur all faces and license plates.
SelectedVehicles: 1992-1995 Pontiac Grand Am — compact with ribbed plastic cladding
1995-1999 Dodge Neon — small rounded economy, friendly face
1994-2001 Dodge Ram — big rig style grille, bold
